title: Zero-Downtime Migration Strategies
description: Learn blue-green schema migration patterns, the Expand and Contract pattern, and avoiding table locks on high-traffic tables.

data.text: In high-availability web applications, deploying database changes cannot involve taking the database offline. A common mistake is renaming a column in a single migration while deploying code simultaneously; during the rolling deployment, old servers crash when querying the old column name, while new servers crash if the migration hasn't finished yet. The **Expand and Contract Pattern** solves this problem completely.

data.caption: Expand and Contract 3-Phase Migration
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Phase 1: Expand] -->|Add new column as nullable| B[Deploy DB Migration]
    B --> C[Deploy App Code: writes to both old & new columns]
    C --> D[Backfill existing rows in background]
    D --> E[Deploy App Code: reads strictly from new column]
    E --> F[Phase 2: Contract] -->|Drop old column| G[Final DB Migration]

data.title: Renaming `fullName` to `firstName` and `lastName` Safely
items: **Step 1 (Expand)**: Add `firstName` and `lastName` as optional columns. Run `prisma migrate deploy`. Both old and new application code continue running without error.
**Step 2 (Dual Write)**: Deploy application update that writes to both `fullName` and the new columns, while continuing to read from `fullName`.
**Step 3 (Backfill)**: Run a background script to parse and populate `firstName` and `lastName` for historical records.
**Step 4 (Switch Read)**: Deploy application update that reads strictly from `firstName` and `lastName`.
**Step 5 (Contract)**: Remove `fullName` from `schema.prisma` and create a migration to drop the column. Run `prisma migrate deploy`.

data.title: PostgreSQL Lock Contention
data.text: Adding a `NOT NULL` constraint without a default value requires an exclusive table lock (`ACCESS EXCLUSIVE`) in PostgreSQL, which can lock the entire table and cause query timeouts on high-traffic applications. Always add columns as nullable first, populate them, and then add constraints.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Never perform breaking schema changes (e.g. column renames/drops) in a single synchronous release.
Use Expand and Contract: Expand the schema, dual-write, backfill, switch reads, and finally contract.
Be mindful of PostgreSQL table-level locks when modifying large tables.
